papers.title: Real-time Bayesian inference at extreme scale: A digital twin for tsunami early warning applied to the Cascadia subduction zone
papers.field: Computational geophysics; Bayesian inverse problems; real-time tsunami forecasting
papers.summary: The authors combine seafloor-pressure observations with a three-dimensional acoustic-gravity model to infer earthquake-driven seafloor motion and predict coastal wave heights with uncertainty. Shift invariance and block-Toeplitz algorithms move expensive PDE solves into one-time offline preparation. The resulting online inference takes less than 0.2 seconds on 512 A100 GPUs for a synthetic Cascadia scenario; the offline wave solver separately scales to 55.5 trillion degrees of freedom on El Capitan.

Each APU integrates 24 Zen4 CPU cores, a CDNA3 GPU and 128 GB HBM3. HPE Slingshot-200 dragonfly interconnect. Scaling experiments used 85-10,880 nodes / 340-43,520 APUs (called GPUs in the paper).

measurements.precision: Double precision
measurements.scope: Online Phase 4 Bayesian parameter inference: strict upper bound (<0.2 s), excluding offline preparation
measurements.scale: 128 Perlmutter nodes / 512 NVIDIA A100 GPUs; 2,416,530 spatial parameter points x 420 temporal steps (~1.015 billion parameters), 252,000 synthetic noisy observations from 600 hypothesized sensors, and 21 forecast locations.
measurements.location: PDF p. 10, section VII.C and Table III (Phase 4); parameter discretization on p. 7.
measurements.measurement_method: Wall time measured using omp_get_wtime after GPU synchronization and MPI_Barrier (section VI.D, p. 8).

Phase 1 alone requires 621 independent PDE solutions totaling about 538 hours on 512 GPUs; later offline phases also precede the online result. measurements.scope: Weak parallel efficiency of the offline acoustic-gravity PDE solver
measurements.scale: 85 to 10,880 nodes / 340 to 43,520 AMD MI300A GPUs; 128-fold increase in GPUs and problem size; largest problem >55.5 trillion DOF (~1.28 billion DOF/APU), using 4.8 PB of memory.

measurements.scale: 128 Perlmutter nodes / 512 NVIDIA A100 GPUs; 2,416,530 spatial parameter points x 420 temporal steps (~1.015 billion parameters), 252,000 synthetic noisy observations from 600 hypothesized sensors, and 21 forecast locations.

papers.title: Ab-initio Quantum Transport with the GW Approximation, 42,240 Atoms, and Sustained Exascale Performance
papers.field: Quantum transport; semiconductor nanodevices; many-body electronic-structure computation
papers.summary: QuaTrEx combines non-equilibrium Green's functions with self-consistent GW electron-interaction calculations to model silicon nanoribbon transistors at experimentally relevant dimensions. A spatial decomposition and recursive Green's-function solver distribute large devices over accelerator ranks. A 42,240-atom case sustains 1,146.037 Pflop/s in FP64 on Frontier, while Alps reaches 342.637 Pflop/s for 46,464 atoms. These are per-iteration application measurements excluding I/O.

papers.title: Breaking the Molecular Dynamics Timescale Barrier Using a Wafer-Scale System
papers.field: Computational materials science; classical molecular dynamics
papers.summary: This work maps each simulated atom to a processor core on a Cerebras wafer-scale engine and uses local dataflow communication to accelerate Embedded Atom Method molecular dynamics. The approach targets the time horizon of a fixed-size simulation, which is limited by communication latency on conventional CPU/GPU clusters. Uniform copper, tungsten and tantalum crystals and a grain-boundary case demonstrate the method; the audited May 2024 version reports measured loop rates for roughly 802,000 atoms and separately models future optimizations and multi-wafer extensions.
